prompt_premise_corrections.premise: Cmajor currently has no ternary, int8, or float16 types.
prompt_premise_corrections.correction: The material shows only that the emitter's getDataType whitelist excludes them and that the converter aborts on FLOAT16 and UINT8. Language-level type support is unverified.

prompt_premise_corrections.premise: A converter flag is distinct from an emitter change.
prompt_premise_corrections.correction: In this codebase onnxToCmajor.py is the emitter; the whitelist lives in the script itself.

primary_blocker.statement: Operator coverage: the shipped Conv processor ignores ONNX pads and has no stride argument, so all 151 DAC convolutions mis-lower regardless of weight type.

scope_verdict.summary: Quantized types are currently out of scope for DAC-class graphs. Float16 is the smallest change (dtype whitelist, operator multiset otherwise unchanged) but is still blocked. Int8 additionally needs new operators, and ternary needs a new representation with no validation path.

known.statement: Release 1.0.3209 implements sixteen processors; Mul, Sin, Pow, ConvTranspose, ArgMax, ReduceL2, ReduceSum, Shape, Expand, and ConstantOfShape are absent.
onnxToCmajor.py emits onnx::operation::<OpType> for every node and does not reject unknown ops.
getDataType whitelists float32, float64, int32, int64, and bool.
The converter aborts on FLOAT16 (decoder fp16) and UINT8 (int8 decoder and encoder).
FP16 adds one Cast; INT8 adds ConvInteger, DynamicQuantizeLinear, DequantizeLinear, MatMulInteger, and Cast, none of which have Cmajor processors.
A 5.39x literal expansion was measured on codebook weights; the full-model inline figures are extrapolated.

claims.statement: Ternary literals would remove the literal-expansion problem.
INT8 would give a 2-4x CPU speedup (generic claim, not measured here).
Ternary retention figures from an external LLM pipeline do not validate Cmajor or audio codecs.

type_system.statement: A float16 type, or load-time promotion to float32.
An int8/uint8 type with literal syntax and cast semantics.
A ternary type or constrained int8 representation with scale metadata.

emitter_lowering.statement: Extend getDataType and handle FLOAT16/UINT8 initializers.
Render literals for each new type.
Unpack ternary weights and apply group scales.

operators.statement: ConvInteger, MatMulInteger, DynamicQuantizeLinear, DequantizeLinear, and Cast processors.
Prerequisite for every type: rewrite Conv to read pads and accept strides.

validation.statement: Codec-quality evaluation with a defined metric and reference; none exists.

open_design_questions.question: Native quantized types, or storage-only types promoted at load?
Scale granularity: per-tensor, per-channel, or per-group.
Can short ternary literals emit as existing int32/float32 literals with no new type?
Which metric and reference decide codec quality?
How can any lowering claim be checked while cmaj does not start?

assumptions_and_corrections.statement: DAC 24 kHz is representative of the codecs in scope.
The 1.14 GB and 487 MB inline figures are extrapolated from 5.39x, not measured.
'Eliminates expansion entirely' for ternary literals is unmeasured; scales add literals.
All claims about Cmajor source rest on the author's notes; the Cmajor repository was not read.
'ONNX Runtime Web handles every op natively' was not tested; only FP16 graphs were run.

verification_limits: cmaj 1.0.3209 did not start in the test environment; nothing was compile-checked and no WASM was produced.
No codec-quality metric was evaluated for any quantized variant.
bottom_line: Ternary weights are currently out of scope for the Cmajor emitter. They require type-system and emitter changes and sit behind an unstarted Conv rewrite. Float16 is the most plausible first step but is unmeasured inside Cmajor.
